[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Building Async Views and WebSockets in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flask has evolved to support modern asynchronous paradigms and real-time communication protocols. This tutorial explores how to leverage Flask async route handlers and implement WebSockets using Flask-Sock."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites and Installation"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"To handle asynchronous requests and WebSocket connections, you need Flask version 2.0 or higher, along with an ASGI server like Uvicorn and the Flask-Sock extension."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"pip install flask uvicorn flask-sock"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Writing Asynchronous Views"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Flask allows you to define route handlers using the async/await syntax. These async views are particularly useful when your application performs non-blocking I/O operations, such as making external HTTP requests or querying asynchronous databases."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
import asyncio

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route('/async-data')
async def async_data():
    await asyncio.sleep(1) # Simulate non-blocking I/O
    return {"message": "Data fetched asynchronously!"}"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Integrating WebSockets with Flask-Sock"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"While native Flask supports async HTTP routes, WebSockets require a persistent, bidirectional connection. Flask-Sock is a lightweight extension that integrates seamlessly with Flask to handle WebSocket endpoints."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from flask_sock import Sock

app = Flask(__name__)
sock = Sock(app)

@sock.route('/echo')
app_echo(sock):
    while True:
        data = sock.receive()
        sock.send(f"Echo: {data}")"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Running the Application with an ASGI Server"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because Flask relies on ASGI to run asynchronous views and WebSockets concurrently, you must use an ASGI server such as Uvicorn instead of the standard built-in Werkzeug development server."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"uvicorn app:app --reload"},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensure your ASGI server points correctly to your application instance (e.g., app:app)."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use async libraries compatible with Python's asyncio event loop within your async views."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Handle WebSocket disconnection exceptions gracefully to prevent memory leaks."}]
